# Native Linux installation
Install PostgreSQL 16+, Python 3.12+, Node 22 and Nginx using your distribution packages. Create a PostgreSQL role/database owned by the institution. Do not expose port 5432 to the Internet.

1. In backend: `python3 -m venv .venv`; activate it; `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
2. Export DATABASE_URL (`postgresql+psycopg://...`), SESSION_SECRET (64 random hex), ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD (14+ characters), PUBLIC_ORIGIN and COOKIE_SECURE=true for HTTPS.
3. Run `python -m app.migrate`, then run `uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000` under a systemd service owned by a dedicated unprivileged user.
4. In frontend: `npm ci && npm run build`. Serve dist with Nginx. Proxy /api to 127.0.0.1:8000; use the supplied nginx.conf as a starting point (replace upstream api with 127.0.0.1).
5. Point your A/AAAA records to the server. Install Certbot, issue a certificate for the verified domain, redirect HTTP to HTTPS and set PUBLIC_ORIGIN to that HTTPS origin. Renew certificates automatically.
6. Restrict the firewall to SSH, HTTP and HTTPS. Keep secrets outside the source tree; enable database backups and test restoration on an isolated database.

No Cloudflare service, ChatGPT login or paid AI subscription is required by this portable runtime. Ordinary VPS/domain costs remain. The existing Sites experience is separately retained in the parent directory.

# Generated DUDOS site
Run `bash ops/install.sh`, inspect .env, then open http://localhost:8080 locally. Pages are persisted in PostgreSQL; use CMS at #cms (React) or /#cms (Next.js). Sign in with ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env. Edit each page and save. Contact enquiries are stored in the same database and visible in CMS. Content is escaped by React; HTML is not executed.

Read project.json and REQUIREMENTS.md before deployment. API integration selections are not activated. Run QA with `python -m pip install playwright && python -m playwright install chromium && python ops/qa.py http://localhost:8080`. QA creates qa-report.json and reports failures; it does not silently approve the site. Enter CMS credentials through environment variables to test sign-in/page editing. Inspect on a real browser before production. Set your domain DNS and HTTPS using ops/native-install.md. No mandatory paid AI service.

## Upgrade and recovery
Back up PostgreSQL using ops/backup.sh before any update. Keep source versions and checksums. Test restore in isolation. The initial schema uses additive creation; later changes require reviewed migration scripts. This package includes application source and dependency lockfiles. Docker builds use npm ci; retain the lockfile for reproducible upgrades.

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Enquiry;
use App\Models\Page;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;

class SiteController extends Controller
{
    private function config(): array
    {
        return config('dudos');
    }

    public function show(Request $request, string $slug = 'home')
    {
        $pages = Page::orderBy('id')->get();
        $page = $pages->firstWhere('slug', $slug) ?? $pages->first();

        return view('site', [
            'config' => $this->config(),
            'pages' => $pages,
            'active' => $slug,
            'page' => $page,
            'authed' => Auth::check(),
            'enquiries' => Auth::check() ? Enquiry::orderByDesc('id')->limit(200)->get() : collect(),
            'message' => $request->session()->pull('message'),
        ]);
    }

    public function cms(Request $request)
    {
        return $this->show($request, 'cms');
    }

    public function login(Request $request)
    {
        $data = $request->validate([
            'email' => 'required|email|max:200',
            'password' => 'required|min:1|max:200',
        ]);

        if (! Auth::attempt(['email' => $data['email'], 'password' => $data['password']])) {
            return back()->with('message', 'Invalid sign-in details');
        }

        $request->session()->regenerate();

        return redirect('/cms')->with('message', 'Signed in');
    }

    public function logout(Request $request)
    {
        Auth::logout();
        $request->session()->invalidate();
        $request->session()->regenerateToken();

        return redirect('/cms')->with('message', 'Signed out');
    }

    public function savePage(Request $request, string $slug)
    {
        if (! Auth::check()) {
            abort(401, 'Sign in to continue');
        }

        $page = Page::where('slug', $slug)->firstOrFail();

        $data = $request->validate([
            'title' => 'required|string|max:200',
            'body' => 'nullable|string|max:50000',
        ]);

        $page->update([
            'title' => $data['title'],
            'body' => $data['body'] ?? '',
            'revision' => $page->revision + 1,
        ]);

        return redirect('/cms')->with('message', 'Page saved');
    }

    public function contact(Request $request)
    {
        // Honeypot field: real visitors never populate it.
        if ($request->filled('website')) {
            return redirect('/contact')->with('message', 'Thank you. Your enquiry has been saved.');
        }

        $data = $request->validate([
            'name' => 'required|string|max:200',
            'email' => 'required|email|max:200',
            'message' => 'required|string|max:3000',
        ]);

        Enquiry::create($data);

        return redirect('/contact')->with('message', 'Thank you. Your enquiry has been saved.');
    }
}

# Generated DUDOS site (Laravel)

Run `bash ops/install.sh`, inspect .env, then open http://localhost:8080 locally. Pages are persisted in MySQL; use the CMS at /cms. Sign in with ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env. Edit each page and save. Contact enquiries are stored in the same database and visible in the CMS. Content is escaped by Blade by default; the generated hero markup is trusted output from your own template, not user input.

Read project.json and REQUIREMENTS.md before deployment. API integration selections are not activated. Migrations and the seeder run automatically on container start (`ops/entrypoint.sh`); the seeder is idempotent — rerunning it never duplicates the admin user or seeded pages. Inspect on a real browser before production. Set your domain DNS and HTTPS using your own reverse proxy in front of port 8080. No mandatory paid AI service.

## Upgrade and recovery
Back up MySQL using `ops/backup.sh` before any update. Keep source versions and checksums. Test restore in isolation with `ops/restore.sh`. This package includes application source and a `composer.lock` for reproducible installs — keep it alongside `composer.json` when you upgrade dependencies (`composer update` regenerates it deliberately; don't hand-edit it).

odoo18.odoo_module/README.md:
# __PROJECT_NAME__ — DUDOS website pages for Odoo 18

This module adds the pages configured in the DUDOS Website Builder to an **existing Odoo 18** instance, as native Website pages built on Odoo's own `website.page` / QWeb view records. It does not install or provision Odoo itself, and it does not create a database — it plugs into a database you already run.

## What this is (and isn't)

- Each configured page becomes a real `website.page` record with its own QWeb view, listed in Odoo's Website app and editable there with Odoo's own drag-and-drop page builder afterward.
- The home page carries the rendered visual direction (colors, layout, hero copy) from the starter template you selected in the builder; other pages are plain content pages with your project's title/body text.
- Pages import **unpublished** (`is_published = False`) by default. Review content, rights and branding, then publish each page from Website > Site > Pages before it becomes publicly visible.
- **Contact / enquiry handling is not included.** Building a custom form controller would duplicate — and likely fight with — Odoo's own mature Website Form and CRM lead-capture building blocks. Add a contact form to the generated Contact page using Odoo's page builder ("+Blocks" > Forms) and route it to CRM or email exactly as you would for any other Odoo Website page.
- No theme, template-marketplace asset, or third-party module is installed. Only the pages, views and menu items listed in `data/`.

## Installation

1. Copy this module's folder into your Odoo `addons_path` (or your custom addons directory), keeping its folder name unchanged.
2. Restart the Odoo service so it picks up the new addon.
3. In Odoo, go to Apps, remove the default "Apps" filter, click "Update Apps List", then search for and install this module.
4. Go to Website > Site > Pages to review the imported pages. Publish each one once you're satisfied with its content.
5. Add navigation, a contact form and any additional blocks using Odoo's own Website builder.

## Upgrading or removing

Uninstalling this module removes the pages, views and menu items it created; it does not touch unrelated Website content. To update content after editing it in Odoo's builder, edit it there directly — reinstalling this module does not overwrite pages you've already customized, since Odoo treats installed data records as protected by default (`noupdate="1"`).
